summary: Palmo Kyi works in the field of Tibetology. She studied under Per Kværne, Hanna Havnevik, and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna and was a research student at the Australian National University circa 1971–1976.

Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) studied at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. A scholar of Indology and history, his posts included vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949) and National Professor of Indology (circa 1959–1972).
Pankaj Tandon specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was mentored by Tom Mallon-McCorgray and held a post at Boston University (attested 2015).

Paolo Visigalli works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Rome, the University of Padua, and the University of Cambridge (circa 2011–2015), and held a post at New York University Shanghai.

Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya (1891–1978) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was Director of the Mithila Institute (circa 1954–1958) and succeeded Shripad Krishna Belvalkar as General Editor of the Mahabharata at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (circa 1961–1972).

Parimal G. Patil specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (circa 1989–1993) and the University of Chicago (circa 1993–2002), and became a Professor at Harvard University circa 2004.

Parul Dave-Mukherji is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and was attested in 2020 as a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Pasang Wangdu (born 1944) works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner, and held a post as Professor at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2006–2014).

Pascale Haag (born 1965) specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat and at Paris Nanterre University under Marie-Claire Gay, holding a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences circa 2006.

Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2006), the University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2008).

Pataraporn Sirikanchana specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a Professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

Patrice Ladwig specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Münster, University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, and held positions at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, served as Curator of Chinese Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, and joined UC Berkeley's History of Art faculty in 1996.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey (born 1947) is a scholar of Sinology and history. She studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University, later holding faculty posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia Fister (born 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas (~1976–1983), where she also taught, before serving as Professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2003–2018).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani specializes in Sinology and Tibetology. She studied at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.
Patrick Arthur Pranke specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.

Patrick Jory works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the Australian National University under Craig J. Reynolds by 1996 and held a post at the University of Queensland (attested 2016).
